title: 37.4 SHINSAI: A 586mm2 Reusable Active TSV Interposer with Programmable Interconnect Fabric and 512Mb 3D Underdeck Memory
problem: Active TSV interposers for 3D chiplet stacking are designed for specific configurations, leading to inflexible interconnect topologies and poor reuse across different chip combinations; orchestrating diverse top-dies with on-interposer memory remains challenging.
motivation: Reducing NRE costs and design complexity in 3D systems requires reusable interposer platforms that adapt to multiple chiplet configurations without redesign.
method: SHINSAI is a programmable physical layer (called an interposer) that connects stacked computer chips together, built in 28nm CMOS with through-silicon vias (tiny wires threaded through the silicon). Inside, it has two routing layers: horizontal 2.5D paths (H-Link) that route connections within the interposer, and vertical 3D paths (V-Link) that connect upward to the stacked chips. It includes 512Mb of on-board SRAM to manage data between chips. Because the routing is programmable rather than hardwired, you can reconfigure how different chips connect without changing the physical hardware, letting the same interposer work with many different chip combinations.
key_novelty: The core innovation is making the interposer's routing programmable so it works with different chip combinations instead of being locked into one configuration.
contributions: Dual-layer NoAI with programmable H-Link/V-Link routing
512Mb underdeck SRAM with flexible bandwidth assignment
Support for diverse chiplet configurations (CPU/accelerator stacks)
primary_theme: Programmable active interposer for flexible chiplet stacking
